current_example.problem: Given the sets $X = \{2, 5, 7, 8\},$ $Y = \{1, 3, 5\},$ and $Z = \{2, 4, 6, 8\},$ find $X \cup Y,$ $Y \cup Z,$ and $Z \cup X.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The union $X \cup Y$ is the set of all elements belonging to either $X$ or $Y,$ or both. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}X\cup Y & =\{2,5,7,8\}\cup \{1,3,5\} \\  & =\{1,2,3,5,7,8\}.\end{aligned}
$$

The union $Y \cup Z$ is the set of all elements belonging to either $Y$ or $Z,$ or both. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Y\cup Z & =\{1,3,5\}\cup \{2,4,6,8\} \\  & =\{1,2,3,4,5,6,8\}.\end{aligned}
$$

The union $Z \cup X$ is the set of all elements belonging to either $Z$ or $X,$ or both. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Z\cup X & =\{2,4,6,8\}\cup \{2,5,7,8\} \\  & =\{2,4,5,6,7,8\}.\end{aligned}
$$
